proposed.explanation: The investor needs 10,000 EGP in cash within three months for a family wedding. Current holdings consist of 200 shares of EFID and 1,000 EGP cash. At the cutoff price of 20.40 EGP per share, selling all 200 shares yields 200 × 20.40 = 4,080 EGP. Adding the existing 1,000 EGP gives a total of 5,080 EGP, which falls short of the 10,000 EGP target by 4,920 EGP. Therefore, selling the EFID shares is the best action available given the portfolio, but the investor will still need to find an additional source of cash (e.g., savings, family support) to meet the full requirement. The decision respects the low willingness to accept losses and low financial ability to withstand losses, as selling at the current price locks in the market value and converts the holding into liquid cash immediately. No financial figures from the EFID reports (revenue, net profit, EPS) are used in this recommendation, as the decision is driven by liquidity needs rather than valuation.
